title: Chemical Equilibrium
seo_title: Grade 12 Physical Sciences: Chemical Equilibrium Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_text: Open and closed systems; reversible reactions and dynamic equilibrium; the equilibrium constant Kc and its expression; calculations with Kc (using a table of moles); Le Chatelier's principle and the effect of concentration, pressure and temperature; the effect of a catalyst; industrial applications such as the Haber process. (summary of CAPS Physical Sciences, Grade 12, Chemistry: Chemical equilibrium)
meta_desc: Free Grade 12 Physical Sciences worksheets (CAPS): dynamic equilibrium, Kc expressions and calculations, Le Chatelier's principle and industrial processes. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: At equilibrium the forward and reverse rates are equal.
key_sub: Only temperature changes the value of Kc.
body_html:
How to think about it

In a closed system a reversible reaction reaches dynamic equilibrium: the forward and reverse reactions continue at the same rate, so the concentrations stay constant. For aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD, Kc = [C]ᶜ[D]ᵈ / [A]ᵃ[B]ᵇ; solids and pure liquids are left out. A large Kc means mostly products.

Le Chatelier's principle: when an equilibrium is disturbed, it shifts to oppose the change. Adding a reactant shifts it to the right; increasing pressure favours the side with fewer moles of gas; increasing temperature favours the endothermic reaction. A catalyst speeds up both reactions equally and does not shift the equilibrium.

Example

N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ (exothermic). Temperature is raised. Effect on the yield of NH₃?

Endothermic direction is favoured.

Answer: it decreases

Example

Write Kc for H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI.

Products over reactants

Answer: [HI]² / ([H₂][I₂])

Common mistakes

  • Thinking reactions stop at equilibrium.
  • Including solids in Kc.
  • Thinking a catalyst increases the yield.

items.q: An engineer wants more SO<sub>3</sub> from making sulfuric acid (contact process): 2SO<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2SO<sub>3</sub>, the energy change = −198 kJ. Which single change increases the amount of SO<sub>3</sub> at equilibrium?
c: The pressure is increased (the container is made smaller).
The pressure is decreased (the container is made larger).
items.e: Left: 3 mol gas, right: 2 mol gas. Higher pressure favours fewer gas moles; lower pressure favours more.

items.q: An engineer wants more HI from a sealed tube of hydrogen and iodine: H<sub>2</sub> + I<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2HI, the energy change = −9 kJ. Which single change increases the amount of HI at equilibrium?
c: The pressure is increased (the container is made smaller).
items.e: the energy change = −9 kJ, so the forward reaction is exothermic. Cooling favours the exothermic direction.

items.e: the energy change = −92 kJ, so the forward reaction is exothermic. Cooling favours the exothermic direction.

items.q: Why is the Haber process run at about 450 °C, even though a lower temperature gives more ammonia?
c: a lower temperature would make the rate too slow; 450 °C is a compromise
items.e: Yield and rate are balanced.
